## Role preferences

::: {.recruiter-faq-toolbar}
Preferred scope, team shape, and working style.

::: {.recruiter-faq-actions}
<button
  class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
  type="button"
  data-details-action="expand"
>
  Expand all
</button>
<button
  class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
  type="button"
  data-details-action="collapse"
>
  Collapse all
</button>
:::
:::

<details>
<summary>What kinds of roles are the best fit?</summary>
<p>
I am strongest in technical roles where I can build, improve, or shape machine learning and AI capabilities. I enjoy working across the full pipeline, especially in high-velocity environments: understanding the problem, designing the approach, building the system, and improving it from real-world feedback. I am also comfortable owning a specific stage of the work in larger organisations.</p>
<p>
Good-fit titles currently include Applied Scientist, Machine Learning Engineer, AI Engineer, Data Scientist, and Analytics Lead, though I care more about the work itself than the title.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>Individual contributor or management track?</summary>
<p>
I am currently prioritising senior individual contributor roles where I can keep my technical edge sharp. I have led small teams before and would consider management opportunities, but only when they remain close to the technical work, problem solving, and delivery.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>What kinds of roles would <u><i>not</i></u> be a good fit?</summary>
<p>
I am less interested in roles centred mainly on product analytics, experiment reporting, dashboards, frequent stakeholder presentations, or one-off analysis pieces. I am looking for work where the main contribution is building durable technical capabilities, not primarily coordinating, reporting, or presenting. </p>
<p>
I am also unlikely to thrive in heavily meeting-driven roles where the day-to-day work is mostly alignment rather than technical problem solving.
</p>
</details>

## Tech stack & skills

::: {.recruiter-faq-toolbar}
Core tools, technical strengths, and complementary skills.

::: {.recruiter-faq-actions}
<button

>

<details>
<summary>Which technologies do you use most often?</summary>
<p>
My core working stack is Python, R, and SQL. I am comfortable moving between exploratory analysis, statistical modelling, machine learning workflows, data pipelines, and production-facing analytics.
</p>
<p>
I have worked across the main cloud platforms: GCP, Azure, and AWS, and have recent experience working with Snowflake as a data warehouse. 
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>What are your strongest technical areas?</summary>
<p>
My strongest areas are applied machine learning, statistical modelling, health and policy analytics, evidence generation, and translating ambiguous questions into usable analytical or ML systems. I am especially strong where the work requires both technical depth and careful interpretation: regulated domains, healthcare data, public-sector evidence, or high-stakes decisions.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>What makes your technical profile distinctive?</summary>
<p>
The distinctive part of my profile is the combination of statistics, economics, applied ML, and production experience. I can help frame the problem, choose a sensible modelling approach, build the workflow, evaluate the evidence, and explain the trade-offs to technical and non-technical audiences.
</p>
<p>
That mix tends to work well in teams that need someone who can bridge research, modelling, engineering, and decision-making rather than sit in only one narrow lane.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>Do you have experience with ML lifecycle and reproducibility?</summary>
<p>
Yes. I have worked across the ML lifecycle, from project scoping and prototyping through to data pipelines, model development, monitoring, and evaluation. I care about reproducibility, version control, clear analytical assumptions, and making models or analyses understandable enough to be used responsibly.
</p>
</details>

## Location & eligibility

::: {.recruiter-faq-toolbar}
Geography, remote work, and right to work considerations.

::: {.recruiter-faq-actions}

<details>
<summary>Where are you based?</summary>
<p>
I am currently based in London, UK, and have the right to work here. I am open to roles based in the UK or fully remote roles based in other locations, as long as they are compatible with my time zone and legal eligibility.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>What work setup is preferred?</summary>
<p>
Hybrid or remote-first roles are typically the best match, with in-person collaboration up to 3 days a week in London.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>Do you have right to work in the UK?</summary>
<p>
Yes, I have the right to work in the UK under the EU Settled Scheme and in EU countries as an Italian national.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>Do you hold any clearance?</summary>
<p>
Although I have held SC clearance in the past, I do not currently hold any active security clearance. I am open to roles that require clearance and would be willing to go through the necessary process if required.
</p>
</details>


## Compensation

::: {.recruiter-faq-toolbar}
How compensation discussions are best handled.

::: {.recruiter-faq-actions}
<button
  class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
  type="button"
  data-details-action="expand"
>
  Expand all
</button>
<button
  class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
  type="button"
  data-details-action="collapse"
>
  Collapse all
</button>
:::
:::

<details>
<summary>What are your compensation expectations?</summary>
<p>
With the usual disclaimer that it will depend heavily on other non-monetary factors as well as benefits, for contract roles I would typically expect a <u><i>minimum</i></u> day rate of around £450 for outside IR35, and £600 for inside IR35. For permanent roles, a total compensation range of around £80k-£120k would be a reasonable starting point for discussions, depending on the factors mentioned above.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>What helps make compensation talks efficient?</summary>
<p>
A sensible range, hiring level, and any location constraints are ideal to share early. That makes it easier to decide quickly whether a process is worth both sides' time.
</p>
</details>

::: {.recruiter-faq-toolbar}
Practical logistics and next-step expectations.

::: {.recruiter-faq-actions}

<details>
<summary>What should recruiters include when reaching out?</summary>
<p>
Please include the role title, company or sector, contract or permanent status, location and remote expectations, compensation range, hiring level, and a short description of the work. That makes it much easier to respond quickly and usefully.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>Are you open to contract and permanent roles?</summary>
<p>
Yes. I am open to both contract and permanent roles, provided the work is a strong fit technically and the expectations are clear.
</p>
</details>

<details>
<summary>How quickly can you decide to proceed/interview?</summary>
<p>
If the role brief, compensation range, location expectations, and hiring level are clear, I can usually give a quick view on whether the opportunity is worth exploring further.
</p>
</details>
